original.reason: “Exactly 2000 prime divisors (all equal to 3)” is satisfied when prime divisors are counted with multiplicity. The induction correctly proves 3^k divides 2^(3^k)+1, so n=3^2000 works.

judgment.reason: It silently changes “prime divisors” to distinct prime divisors. Under the intended multiplicity count, 3^2000 has 2000 prime divisors.
It incorrectly imposes distinctness on the prime-divisor count and therefore rejects a valid construction.
Its claimed cardinality defect relies on counting only distinct primes, contrary to the construction’s stated multiplicity interpretation.
It erroneously treats the theorem as requiring 2000 distinct prime divisors; n=3^2000 satisfies the stated count with multiplicity.
